Let \(c=3^{2/(2k-1)}\) (interpreting the recurrence’s \(x\) as \(k\)). Since  
\[
S_{n+1}=S_n+a_{n+1}=S_n+(c-1)S_n+3=cS_n+3,
\]
with \(S_1=3\), we get
\[
S_n=3\frac{c^n-1}{c-1}.
\]
Thus
\[
a_n=S_n-S_{n-1}=3c^{n-1}.
\]
So
\[
a_1a_2\cdots a_n=3^n c^{n(n-1)/2},
\]
and
\[
b_n=1+\frac{n-1}{2}\log_3 c
=1+\frac{n-1}{2k-1}.
\]
Hence
\[
b_i-\frac32=\frac{i-1}{2k-1}-\frac12
=\frac{2i-2k-1}{2(2k-1)}.
\]
The terms are negative for \(i=1,\dots,k\) and positive for \(i=k+1,\dots,2k\). Therefore
\[
T_k=\frac{1}{2(2k-1)}\left(\sum_{i=1}^k(2k+1-2i)+\sum_{i=k+1}^{2k}(2i-2k-1)\right)
=\frac{k^2}{2k-1}.
\]
Since \(\gcd(k,2k-1)=1\), the condition \(T_k\in\mathbb Z_+\) requires \(2k-1\mid k^2\), so \(2k-1=1\). Thus \(k=1\).

\[
\boxed{1}
\]
